scenario_text: Track an acute outbreak in a closed, normalized population divided into susceptible, infectious, and recovered fractions. New infections transfer individuals from the susceptible fraction to the infectious fraction through homogeneous person-to-person contact, while recovery transfers infectious individuals to the recovered fraction. The symbolic regression target is the instantaneous change in infectious prevalence over time. Observations span the rise, peak, and decline of a single outbreak under fixed transmission and recovery conditions.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.saturation_strength: 0 <= saturation_strength <= 1/I_initial_scale with nonnegative values; values near 0 recover mass-action transmission, larger values activate visible suppression when I becomes appreciable

derivation_notes: The bilinear mass-action infection term is refined by allowing effective transmission per infectious individual to decrease with infectious prevalence, representing repeated contacts, crowding, or spontaneous caution within the same closed outbreak. This keeps the same states and recovery law but changes the transmission response from linear in I to saturating in I.
change_summary: The assumption of strictly mass-action bilinear incidence is relaxed to a prevalence-saturating incidence law. This introduces downward curvature in infectious growth at higher I while preserving the parent model when saturation_strength approaches zero.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Transmission is represented by strictly mass-action bilinear incidence transmission_rate*S*I with constant marginal transmission contribution from each additional infectious individual.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Prevalence-dependent saturation of effective transmission due to repeated contacts, contact crowding, or spontaneous caution during an acute outbreak in a closed population.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As saturation_strength -> 0, the incidence term transmission_rate*S*I/(1 + saturation_strength*I) converges to transmission_rate*S*I and the full system reduces to the parent SIR model.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps observed states to infectious growth as dI_dt = I*(transmission_rate*S - recovery_rate), so transmission increases linearly with S at one fixed gain transmission_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the constant-per-contact transmission assumption so effective transmission weakens as infectious prevalence rises, making dI_dt depend on a nonlinear incidence term in S and I rather than a single linear gain on S*I.
response_change.observable_effect: At the same susceptible fraction S, larger I produces less-than-proportional additional infection pressure, so the rise and approach to peak are flatter than the parent predicts under higher-prevalence portions of the same outbreak trajectory.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when infectious prevalence reaches non-negligible levels during the same closed-outbreak trajectory, so repeated infectious contacts, local crowding, or spontaneous contact reduction become consequential; effect is weak as I -> 0 and strongest around the outbreak rise and near peak.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early growth at low I remains close to bilinear S*I transmission, while later points at larger I show suppressed growth relative to the parent. In holdout segments spanning higher-prevalence portions, the same mechanism extends this flattening without changing recovery structure.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing prevalence-dependent suppression strength, the refined incidence law reduces continuously to transmission_rate*S*I and recovers the parent SIR model.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Prevalence-dependent saturation of effective transmission due to repeated contacts, contact crowding, or spontaneous caution during an acute outbreak in a closed population.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement changes the target mapping itself by modulating the transmission process with the state-dependent factor 1/(1 + saturation_strength*I), creating curvature in dI_dt as a function of I at fixed S. This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because no single constant transmission_rate can match both low-I near-bilinear growth and high-I suppressed growth over the same trajectory.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Transmission and recovery conditions are constant over time, with transmission represented by strictly mass-action bilinear incidence transmission_rate*S*I.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Transmission remains under fixed external conditions but effective infection generation saturates with infectious prevalence through a prevalence-dependent modulation of the mass-action term.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: As saturation_strength -> 0, transmission_rate*S*I/(1 + saturation_strength*I) - recovery_rate*I reduces to transmission_rate*S*I - recovery_rate*I.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compared on the observed states alone, the parent predicts dI_dt/I = transmission_rate*S - recovery_rate, linear in S and independent of any extra curvature in I beyond the overall factor I. The child predicts dI_dt = transmission_rate*S*I/(1 + saturation_strength*I) - recovery_rate*I, so for similar S values along the trajectory, increasing I depresses the incremental transmission contribution and flattens growth before and around the peak. This changed target mapping is observable when I is appreciable; it is not merely a change to auxiliary trajectories.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting transmission_rate and recovery_rate with one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce both regimes because the parent enforces one bilinear gain on S*I everywhere. Lowering transmission_rate enough to fit high-I suppression would underpredict early low-I growth, while fitting early growth would overpredict transmission later when I is larger. The discrepancy appears under the same fixed-parameter outbreak trajectory and therefore cannot be absorbed by parameter retuning alone.

evolution_plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing prevalence-dependent suppression strength, the refined incidence law reduces continuously to transmission_rate*S*I and recovers the parent SIR model.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes each additional infectious individual contributes the same marginal transmission opportunity regardless of how prevalent infection already is.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Transmission and recovery conditions are constant over time, with transmission represented by strictly mass-action bilinear incidence transmission_rate*S*I.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Prevalence-dependent saturation of effective transmission due to repeated contacts, contact crowding, or spontaneous caution during an acute outbreak in a closed population.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the mathematical form of transmission, not to add a separate new process. The parent target mapping uses a single bilinear gain: at fixed recovery_rate and fixed observed S, dI_dt changes linearly with I through transmission_rate*S*I. That is a single_gain shortcut. A scientifically admissible refinement is prevalence-dependent transmission saturation, where the infection term bends downward as I increases. The varied condition is infectious prevalence I along the observed outbreak trajectory, with transmission_rate and recovery_rate held fixed as parameters and no new intervention required. The concrete contrast is that two times with similar S but different I can have less-than-proportional transmission at higher I, giving reduced slope and stronger downward curvature in dI_dt versus I than the parent allows. This is observable only when I becomes appreciable; near outbreak start with I very small, the child should closely match the parent, which also makes the refinement a natural continuation rather than a disconnected replacement. No new state is necessary because the intended effect can be expressed directly as a nonlinear dependence on already observed S and I.

derivation_notes: The constant-hazard recovery assumption is relaxed by introducing a later infectious subphase whose occupancy carries the recoverable burden, so total infectious prevalence retains memory of recent incidence composition. A finite-capacity removal response is applied to that subphase to match the required saturating embedding while preserving recovery of the parent behavior when the subphase rapidly tracks total I and phase_saturation is negligible.
change_summary: Recovery no longer removes a fixed fraction of total I uniformly; instead, removal depends on occupancy of a later infectious phase that evolves over time. This creates phase-dependent turnover and can separate rising-side and falling-side dI_dt values at similar I within the same outbreak.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Recovery that removes infectious individuals at a constant per-capita rate regardless of time since becoming infectious.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Stage-structured infectiousness or symptom progression causing recovery/removal to depend on occupancy of an infectious subphase rather than uniformly on total current prevalence.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When phase_progression_rate is fast enough that I_phase approximately equals I and phase_saturation = 0, the successor reduces to the parent recovery law recovery_rate*I.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps (S,I) to dI_dt with a time-invariant recovery loss recovery_rate*I, so for fixed transmission parameters the decline rate at a given I depends only on S through the infection term and cannot change systematically with time spent infected.
response_change.child_relation: Relax constant per-capita recovery by allowing recovery pressure to evolve during the outbreak through one additional latent disease-phase state, so dI_dt depends on both current prevalence and the current occupancy of a slower or faster recovery phase rather than only on total I.
response_change.observable_effect: During outbreaks with the same initial conditions and fixed transmission conditions, the child can produce a sharper or delayed turnover and a decline rate at matched I that differs between the rising and falling sides of the epidemic because infectious individuals are not all equally recoverable at every moment.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the infectious-period distribution is not approximately exponential, so the outbreak timescale is comparable to the mean infectious duration and phase structure becomes appreciable across the rise, peak, and decline under the given initial condition.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism appears as asymmetric growth and decay around the peak at similar I values; in holdout it extends to shifted peak timing and altered post-peak steepness without changing the closed-population SIR setting.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the added infectious phase collapses to an exponential-memory description, making total infectious individuals recover with an effectively constant per-capita rate recovery_rate.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A non-exponential infectious-period effect cannot be represented with the existing total-I state alone because any model using only current S and I with fixed parameters remains memoryless in I; one additional state is needed to encode infectious-phase occupancy that feeds back on dI_dt.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Stage-structured progression to a preferentially recoverable infectious subphase with finite-capacity removal
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Stage-structured infectiousness or symptom progression causing recovery/removal to depend on occupancy of an infectious subphase rather than uniformly on total current prevalence.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The target derivative now depends on a hidden phase-occupancy state with its own dynamics, so matching dI_dt requires reconstructing outbreak memory rather than retuning a single constant recovery coefficient. The added saturation in phase-dependent removal changes how turnover sharpens as recoverable occupancy accumulates, which is structurally different from a coefficient-only correction.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Recovery that removes infectious individuals at a constant per-capita rate regardless of time since becoming infectious.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Recovery/removal acts predominantly on a later infectious subphase whose occupancy evolves during the outbreak and can itself show finite-capacity saturation in effective removal.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When phase_progression_rate is large enough that I_phase tracks I and phase_saturation = 0, the child recovery term becomes recovery_rate*I and the parent equation is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Along a single outbreak trajectory under fixed transmission and initial conditions, points with similar I but different epidemic phase can have different dI_dt because I_phase lags incidence history. This is strongest when I_phase accumulates appreciably near and after the peak, producing shifted turnover timing or steeper/shallower decline than the parent's unique (S,I) mapping permits.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set still imposes one memoryless mapping from current (S,I) to dI_dt, so it cannot generate different recovery pressure at matched I values on the rising versus falling limbs except through S alone. When phase occupancy history changes recovery loss independently of the current total I, no global retuning of transmission_rate, recovery_rate, and saturation_strength can reproduce that hysteresis-like asymmetry across the observed outbreak.

evolution_plan.promotion_reason: A non-exponential infectious-period effect cannot be represented with the existing total-I state alone because any model using only current S and I with fixed parameters remains memoryless in I; one additional state is needed to encode infectious-phase occupancy that feeds back on dI_dt.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model treats all infectious individuals as having the same instantaneous recovery hazard, omitting disease-age or phase structure within the infectious class.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Recovery that removes infectious individuals at a constant per-capita rate regardless of time since becoming infectious.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Stage-structured infectiousness or symptom progression causing recovery/removal to depend on occupancy of an infectious subphase rather than uniformly on total current prevalence.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the exponential infectious-period assumption. The parent target mapping is memoryless: with transmission_rate, recovery_rate, and saturation_strength fixed, dI_dt at any observed (S,I) is fully determined, so matched (S,I) points on the ascending and descending limbs must have the same instantaneous derivative. That is a single-phase shortcut. A stage-structured infectious class changes the target mapping itself, not merely auxiliary trajectories, because the loss term from I can depend on how many infectious individuals occupy an early versus late subphase. Varying epidemic time along the observed single outbreak while holding the transmission and saturation parameters fixed, the child can show a different decline steepness or turnover timing at the same approximate I due to latent phase occupancy accumulated from prior incidence. This contrast is admissible when the infectious-period distribution is meaningfully non-exponential over the outbreak window; if the distribution is close to exponential, the added state may be weakly identifiable and the parent becomes an adequate approximation. The scientific continuation path is the limit where phase structure collapses and total I again recovers with constant per-capita rate.

derivation_notes: The transmission-saturation law is refined so that late-stage infectious occupancy contributes directly to effective contact suppression, representing stronger behavioral limitation or reduced contact-generating activity when more infections have progressed into the later phase. No new state is needed because the relevant composition variable I_phase is already present and observed within the closed ODE system.
change_summary: Changed the transmission denominator from a function of I alone to a joint function of I and I_phase. This makes the scored target mapping composition-dependent: at the same S and I, larger I_phase now lowers infection influx and hence dI_dt.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The transmission saturation denominator is a function of I alone and is independent of infectious-stage composition.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Stage-composition-dependent effective transmission, where accumulation in the later infectious subphase modifies the saturation of transmission beyond what is explained by total prevalence alone.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when transmission saturation is insensitive to infectious-stage composition, i.e. when the added I_phase contribution inside the saturation law is neglected.

response_change.parent_relation: The current target mapping uses transmission_rate*S*I/(1 + saturation_strength*I), so prevalence-dependent transmission saturation depends only on total infectious prevalence I and not on how much of that prevalence has progressed into the later infectious subphase.
response_change.child_relation: Refine the transmission saturation assumption so the effective infection term depends on both I and I_phase, allowing the same total I to generate different dI_dt when the infectious pool is compositionally shifted toward later-stage cases that more strongly suppress effective contact or transmission.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched S and total I, outbreaks observed on the downslope or near the peak with larger I_phase would show weaker infection growth than early-rise outbreaks with smaller I_phase; the parent cannot express this composition-dependent split because its infection term is fixed by I alone.

evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where transmission saturation depends only on total I and is insensitive to infectious-stage composition.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Stage-composition-dependent effective transmission, where accumulation in the later infectious subphase modifies the saturation of transmission beyond what is explained by total prevalence alone.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the transmission contribution is no longer determined by S and I alone; it now changes across trajectories with identical S and I but different I_phase, creating a genuine joint dependence in the scored target law.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The transmission saturation denominator is a function of I alone and is independent of infectious-stage composition.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Transmission saturation depends jointly on total infectious prevalence and later-phase occupancy, so late-stage cases contribute extra suppression of effective transmission.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: When the saturation law is taken to depend only on I and not on I_phase, the parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For matched S and I during the observed outbreak, dI_dt is lower when I_phase is larger because the infection influx is additionally saturated by I_phase; this split is most visible near the peak and downslope where I_phase has accumulated while I remains appreciable.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast across low- versus high-I_phase conditions at the same S and I, because in the parent the infection term is exactly fixed by S and I and all I_phase influence enters only through removal. Retuning transmission_rate or saturation_strength changes the common S,I response for all compositions rather than creating a composition-specific transmission split.

evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The transmission saturation denominator is a function of I alone and is independent of infectious-stage composition.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Stage-composition-dependent effective transmission, where accumulation in the later infectious subphase modifies the saturation of transmission beyond what is explained by total prevalence alone.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase transmission assumption, not to add a wholly new process. The parent already includes stage structure in recovery through I_phase but keeps transmission saturation tied only to aggregate I. In an acute outbreak, individuals in later infectious stages may be more symptomatic, less mobile, more likely to self-isolate, or otherwise less effective at sustaining transmission-generating contact. Holding transmission_rate, recovery_rate, and the closed-population setting fixed, vary the within-outbreak condition represented by I_phase at matched S and I. The parent predicts the same incidence contribution whenever S and I match, because I_phase affects dI_dt only through the recovery term. The child would instead produce lower infection influx when I_phase is larger, changing the target mapping itself rather than only auxiliary trajectories. This contrast is admissible under the current observation protocol because I_phase is an observed state supplied to the solver and naturally increases after the early growth phase through progression. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce a systematic split in the infection term at matched S and I across low-versus-high I_phase conditions, because its transmission contribution has no I_phase dependence at all. The limitation is that this effect is weak when I is very small or when I_phase remains near zero, so it is mainly visible around intermediate-to-high prevalence and later outbreak stages.

scenario_text: Track an acute outbreak in a closed, normalized population divided into susceptible, infectious, and recovered fractions.
